props.title: Iron Man
props.initialSlug: Billionaire builds supersuit to fight evil and save world

sections.content: Iron Man revolutionized superhero cinema and launched the Marvel Cinematic Universe with Robert Downey Jr.'s perfect portrayal of Tony Stark. The film brilliantly updates the Cold War-era comics character for the War on Terror age, grounding the fantastical elements in contemporary geopolitics. Director Jon Favreau struck gold by focusing on Stark's character development from arrogant weapons dealer to conscious hero, while pioneering the MCU's signature blend of humor and action. The practical effects mixed with CGI created a tangible feel that later superhero films struggled to match.

sections.content: The success of Iron Man transformed Hollywood's approach to shared universes. While Superman (1978) and Batman (1989) were standalone blockbusters, Iron Man's post-credits Nick Fury scene created a template for interconnected storytelling that everyone from Universal's Dark Universe to DC's Extended Universe tried to replicate. The film's mix of military hardware and sci-fi technology influenced Edge of Tomorrow (2014) and Pacific Rim (2013).

Tony Stark's character arc set a new standard for superhero origin stories. Unlike the radioactive accidents or mystic gifts of earlier heroes, Stark's transformation comes through personal choice and technological innovation. This approach influenced later tech-based heroes in Ant-Man (2015) and Black Panther (2018), while the focus on the hero's flaws and redemption arc became a Marvel staple. sections.content: The film's approach to visual effects created a new template for superhero films. By mixing practical suits with CGI enhancements, Iron Man achieved a tangible feel that pure CGI characters like Green Lantern (2011) couldn't match. The HUD interfaces inside Iron Man's helmet influenced sci-fi UI design in films like Oblivion (2013) and Guardians of the Galaxy (2014).
